# A file nobody wrote, committed by a flag nobody thought about

CI refused this delivery because `AGENTS.md:74` links to
`docs/tickets/SEEN-092-sync-the-harness-skill-to-Codex-and-codex.md`, which does not exist. The real
file is `...-to-claude-code-and-codex.md`.

The file is repowise's managed Codex entry point, written by `repowise agents add --target=codex`
during SEEN-098. It is `CLAUDE.md` with "Claude Code" replaced by "Codex" everywhere, by string
substitution with no idea what the strings are. So the title became "Seen: Codex entry point", which is
fine; a ticket's filename inside a link became `...-to-Codex-and-codex.md`, which is broken; its title
became "Sync the harness skill to Codex and Codex", which is nonsense; and the branch rule became
`Codex/<ticket-id>-…`, which is worse than nonsense, because a Codex session following it would branch
with a prefix every writing command in this harness refuses.

`repowise init` was run with `--no-agents` in SEEN-098 for exactly this reason. `agents add` generates
it anyway.

**How it got committed is the part worth keeping.** It sat untracked in the tree from 24 September
until `git add -A` in this ticket's park commit swept it in. Nobody read it. The rule it breaks is one
this session has had in front of it all day: before overwriting or committing, look at the target.
`git add -A` is convenient and it is how an unread file gets a commit message that says something else.

It is removed and gitignored. Codex reads `.agents/skills/seen-harness/SKILL.md`, which `sync`
generates from `docs/harness/skill.md` and `doctor` checks for drift, and that is the file that should
be telling a Codex session how to work.

The link checker caught it. That check exists because SEEN-086 decided a broken link in a document the
assistants read is a defect, and this is the first time it has earned its place.
